title: Coroutine adapter for streaming chat + telemetry-friendly event synthesis
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current Python SDK streaming APIs expose low-level event pumps and callback registries that are powerful but ergonomically heavy for common patterns (coroutine consumption, simple async iteration, and backpressure-aware consumers). Teams building conversational UIs and server-side routers repeatedly implement small adapters: resumable checkpointing, coalescing partial tokens into typed events, and attaching per-event telemetry (latency, token counts, error codes).

Goal: Provide a lightweight coroutine adapter that: 1) enables async for/async with patterns for streaming chat completions; 2) synthesizes a stable, typed event stream (MessageStart, Token, Delta, FunctionCall, MessageEnd, Error) rather than raw protocol fragments; 3) emits telemetry hooks per logical event and aggregates per-stream metrics; 4) offers clear retry/backoff semantics for idempotent replays and resumed streams. The surface should minimize ceremony for app developers and be compatible with existing lower-level streaming primitives so advanced users can opt-in to full control.
acceptance_criteria:
- New coroutine adapter API available: `async with client.stream_chat(...) as convo:` and `async for msg in convo:` works and yields typed event objects.
- Event synthesis produces stable event types with deterministic ordering across partials (no duplicate MessageStart, Token edges preserved).
- Telemetry hooks: per-event callback and aggregated metrics (tokens_emitted, avg_token_latency_ms, resume_attempts) emitted to the Console trace and available to SDK telemetry collectors.
- Retry semantics: consumer-visible retry reason codes and a resume token mechanism allowing at-most-once reprocessing when resumed with server checkpoint.
- Backpressure: built-in bounded buffer with configurable max_inflight_events and sensible defaults; example in docs shows how to lower buffer for low-memory environments.
- Complete unit/integration tests covering partial token assembly, function call boundaries, error-in-the-middle and successful resume flows.
- Example notebook and reference app updated and linked in ticket comments.
design_notes:
- Event model: use small immutable dataclasses (but SDK will expose `TypedEvent` wrappers in a stable enum-like mapping). Types: `StreamOpen`, `MessageStart(role, meta)`, `Token(text, index, is_final)`, `FunctionCall(name, args)`, `MessageEnd`, `StreamClose`, `StreamError(code, message)`.
- Synthesis rules: tokens receive monotonically increasing index within a message. FunctionCall may arrive mid-token stream; synthesize a synthetic MessageEnd before FunctionCall and resume new message after call return.
- Telemetry design: emit lightweight per-event envelope with fields (event_type, timestamp_ms, token_delta, source_model, shard_id). Provide a pluggable `telemetry_sink` param defaulting to no-op; Console wiring in later release will consume these.
- Retry semantics: two modes: optimistic-resume (client supplies last_token_index) and server-anchored-checkpoint (server provides checkpoint_id to resume). Default to optimistic-resume with exponential backoff capped at 3 attempts.
- Backpressure: internal asyncio.Queue with default maxsize=128; when full, the adapter yields control to caller (await) and records `backpressure_pause_ms` metric. Provide explicit `drop_policy` option for ultra-low-memory use-cases.
implementation_plan: 1) Define typed event schema and serialization parity tests against existing streaming wire protocol.
2) Implement coroutine adapter wrapper over current stream primitives; expose `stream_chat` context manager and async iterator.
3) Add token-coalescer and boundary detector for function calls and role transitions.
4) Integrate telemetry hooks and create minimal SDK telemetry interface.
5) Implement resume token exchange and retry coordinator with configuration knobs.
6) Add unit tests and a few end-to-end tests using the local dev runtime harness.
7) Author docs, examples, and a short notebook demo for console and reference app.
8) Internal dogfood: migrate 1 internal sample app to the adapter and validate behavior under load.
9) Cut feature flag gated release to `alpha` channel for early adopters, follow with GA when metrics stable.
10) Post-launch: collect developer feedback and iterate on ergonomics (naming/param defaults).
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for each event type and for token coalescing edge cases (split tokens, multi-functioncall).
- Integration tests simulating: normal stream, intermittent network drops with resume, server checkpoint resume, mid-message error.
- Load test: open 500 concurrent streams with small batch sizes, assert memory usage and backpressure metrics remain within thresholds.
- Fuzz harness: random partial events to ensure adapter fails gracefully and emits StreamError with actionable code.
- Manual UX: follow notebook to build a toy chat UI and verify `async for` iteration behaves when consumer deliberately sleeps to test backpressure.
rollout_plan:
- Feature gated behind `python_streaming_adapter` feature flag.
- Alpha release to SDK nightly wheel and internal `sdk-dogfood` team.
- Monitor telemetry: resume_attempts, avg_token_latency_ms, backpressure_pause_ms for 2 weeks.
- If stable, promote to beta in next minor SDK release; add docs to quickstart and migration guide.
- Deprecation: leave old low-level APIs untouched; provide migration examples and a shim for teams that rely on raw events.
